instruction: Load the unpacked extension from /home/user/Desktop/ into Chrome and check that its description reads 'Base Level Extension'.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Task requires loading the unpacked extension and verifying its description field matches 'Base Level Extension' (from manifest.json). The getter reads Chrome Preferences to find the extension by name and extract its description field. The metric checks for exact match.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts extension description from Chrome Preferences file by matching extension name 'Hello Extensions'
Metric correctly handles expected parameter structure (expected IS the rules dict when type='rule', not {'rules': {...}})
Metric performs exact string comparison between result and expected description 'Base Level Extension'
Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts description string -> metric compares against expected value
Edge cases handled properly: missing extension, missing description field, JSON parsing errors, case-insensitive name matching
Implicit verification of installation: extension must be installed to appear in Preferences with description field
Minor semantic gap: evaluator doesn't explicitly verify extension is enabled/active, only that it exists in Preferences with correct description
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding explicit check for extension state (enabled/disabled) in Chrome Preferences to fully verify installation
Could verify extension path matches /home/user/Desktop/ location to ensure correct extension source
